newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas tracks naphtha ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas tracks naphtha ends lower.

text.p: Naphtha prices on Wednessday plunged with weaker crude, with gasoline following in line in the absence of firm talk ahead of Taiwan's tender, traders said.
Naphtha June swaps plunged by 70 cents per barrel from $21.00/$21.30 with the contango to July widening to 20 cents from 10-15 cents.
Saudi Aramco was rumoured offering spot cargoes of 400,000-tonnes of A-180 and Jubail lifting June-September.
Sources said the cargoes were being offered at around $17-$19 per tonne fob, higher than the term price of $15-$17 for second-half of 1997 supplies, just concluded last month.

But Abu Dhabi National Oil Co's (ADNOC) term naphtha buyers have to bid higher than the Aramco premium, at $19 to $20 per tonne fob over the ADNOC formula for one-year term supplies of 500,000 -700,000 tonnes of naphtha starting in July, traders said.
Traders also said that one of the five potential buyers is likely to have submitted two different prices, $20.00 over the formula for pentane-plus and a $16.00 premium for low sulphur naphtha.

ADNOC initially offered $22.50 over the formula, a jump from the $6.80 premium three Japanese trading houses, one Japanese refiner and one South Korean petrochemical firm currently pay for term supplies ending in June.
The Singapore fob gasoline market was silent ahead of the close of Taiwan's and India's import tenders on Wednesday and valid for two days.
"There is no action...it is too close to the close of Taiwan," a trader said.
Traders were mixed on the expected response to Taiwan's tender for 95-octane unleaded reformate for July 16-30.
"The market is looking more balanced and sellers will not be so aggressive...offers are likely to be in the high $25's," one trader said.
But another said "those who have to place barrels will go in pretty aggressively."
"In the absence of Taiwan's results, Saudi Aramco's bid is quite a reflection of the market levels," a trader said.
Traders said Aramco was bidding for 30,000 tonnes of 95-octane unleaded gasoline for delivery to Ras Tanura in the second-half of June at $3.50 per barrel over Singapore naphtha spot quotes, c-and-f.
On a netback, this would be equivalent of a premium of $2.50 fob Singapore.
A Chinese cargo of around 200,000-barrels of 93-octane unleaded gasoline lifting June 16-30 was heard sold $1.50 over Singapore naphtha quotes, fob Dalian.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
